newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast gasolines ease on NYMEX, thin talk.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast gasolines ease on NYMEX, thin talk.

text.p: U.S. West Coast gasolines fell under pressure from NYMEX, with dealers slow to begin trade after a two-day industry conference and little liquidity expected all day.
November unleaded gasoline prices hit 62.10 by 1340 EDT/1740 GMT, off 0.12 from Tuesday, after falling as low as 61.80 cents a gallon on NYMEX.
Values dropped after weekly inventory reports from the industry and government showed growing supply.
API data showed stocks of gasoline nationwide rose 2.27 million last week to 197.1 million barrels.
Early Wednesday, U.S. Energy Information Administration released its weekly inventory report which showed gasoline in storage climbed 4.2 million barrels to 197.7 million barrels.
Prices for CARB gasoline in Los Angeles slipped between 1.50 and 1.00 cent to 64.50/66.00 cents, under pressure from NYMEX.
Conventional grade gasoline in L.A. edged down a half cent to 70.50/71.50 cents a gallon.
Meanwhile, San Francisco grades stayed 1.50 lower versus L.A. after easing from L.A. levels Tuesday.
Among distillates, CARB diesel held strong at 80/82 cents a gallon, after refiners cut back production last month to process better-priced jet fuel.
"Probably within two weeks it'll start fading out as people switch over production," to CARB again, one trader said.
